claims.text: Mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn can be investigated by systematic tensile and hardness testing across multiple temperatures and strain rates.
FeNiCrMn will exhibit an enhanced combination of strength and ductility under an appropriate range of temperatures and strain rates relative to a single ambient or fixed condition.
The enhanced strength–ductility combination in FeNiCrMn will result from evolving dislocation substructures and deformation twinning.
The tested FeNiCrMn specimens will be solution-annealed or as-cast and have a homogeneous grain structure.
Dislocation networks evolve as a function of strain and temperature.
Deformation twins evolve as a function of strain and temperature.
Secondary-phase precipitates may evolve as a function of strain and temperature in FeNiCrMn.
Increasing temperature and strain activates additional slip systems and twinning mechanisms in FeNiCrMn.
Slip and twinning can synergistically alter work hardening, ductility, strength, and fracture behavior.
FeNiCrMn will attain higher yield strength over a specific temperature range than under ambient-condition testing.
FeNiCrMn will attain higher ductility over a specific temperature range than under ambient-condition testing.
At very high temperatures, FeNiCrMn may soften because of microstructural coarsening or phase changes.
Excessively high temperatures may reduce strengthening and ductility improvements through grain growth or phase transformation.
Ambient-condition FeNiCrMn properties can be benchmarked against literature data for Co-containing Cantor-type HEAs.
The exact temperature and strain-rate thresholds for peak FeNiCrMn performance are not established.
